newsitem.title: USA: Paragon sees pressures, prices hurting 97.
newsitem.headline: Paragon sees pressures, prices hurting 97.

text.p: Paragon Trade Brands Inc said Friday it expected new competitive pressures and rising material prices and the cost of significant product and packaging innovations to reduce 1997 Baby Diaper business earnings to below 1996 levels.
In addition, the company said it expected to bear increased costs associated with patent litigation, upgrading information technology and new business initiatives.

Earlier today, the company reported adjusted net earnings for the Baby Diaper business of $9.0 million, or $0.75 per share, for the fourth quarter. This excludes charges associated with Paragon's corporate relocation, the integration of Pope & Talbot's disposable diaper business and feminine care start-up losses. Including these charges, the company reported net earnings of $5.9 million, or $0.49 per share, for the quarter compared to $3.6 million, or $0.31 per share, for the fourth quarter ended December 31, 1995. Net sales for the quarter were $142.4 million compared to $133.5 million for the same period last year.

For the twelve months ended December 29, 1996, the Baby Diaper business reported adjusted net earnings of $36.6 million, or $3.05 per share, compared to $6.4 million, or $.55 per share, for the year ended December 31, 1995. This excludes charges in both periods associated with Paragon's corporate relocation, the integration of Pope & Talbot's disposable diaper business, restructuring and feminine care start-up losses. Including these charges, the Company reported net earnings of $21.1 million, or $1.76 per share, for the year compared to a net loss of $3.4 million, or $.29 per share, for the year ended December 31, 1995. Net sales for the twelve months were $581.9 million compared to $518.8 million for the year ended December 31, 1995.
